name: scan0007-text-0182
text: Introductory Note.

name: scan0007-text-0183
text: The Liberty engine is of the ungeared twelve-

name: scan0007-text-0184
text: cylinder Vee type, with cylinders set at 45°. The bore

name: scan0007-text-0185
text: is 5 in. (127 mm.), and the stroke 7 in. (177.8 mm.). The

name: scan0007-text-0186
text: “dry” weight is 820 lbs. The engine is constructed in two

name: scan0007-text-0187
text: models, the army type having a higher compression

name: scan0007-text-0188
text: ratio (5.3 : 1) than the naval type (4.78 : 1); the maximum

name: scan0007-text-0189
text: r.p.m. of both types are 1750, at which speed 425

name: scan0007-text-0190
text: b.h.p. is developed by the army type, its normal b.h.p.

name: scan0007-text-0191
text: being 405 at 1650 r.p.m. The naval type is not used in

name: scan0007-text-0192
text: the British Service at present; it gives 396 h.p. at 1,650

name: scan0007-text-0193
text: r.p.m.

name: scan0007-text-0194
text: The water-cooled cylinders are constructed from

name: scan0007-text-0195
text: steel tube with welded jackets: there are two valves per

name: scan0007-text-0196
text: cylinder.

name: scan0007-text-0197
text: The pistons, cylinders, and gudgeon pins are lubri-

name: scan0007-text-0198
text: cated by splash. Oil is pressure-fed to the rest of the

name: scan0007-text-0199
text: engine, including the camshafts. The sump is scavenged

name: scan0007-text-0200
text: by a three-pinion pump combined in a unit with the pres-

name: scan0007-text-0201
text: sure pump, and located in the rear oil well.

name: scan0007-text-0202
text: Ignition is by the Delco system. A twelve-point

name: scan0007-text-0203
text: distributor, embodying two contact breakers in parallel,

name: scan0007-text-0204
text: is mounted on the rear end of each camshaft, and supplied

name: scan0007-text-0205
text: with current for starting and at low engine speeds by

name: scan0007-text-0206
text: an accumulator. When the engine attains 650 r.p.m.,

name: scan0007-text-0207
text: the current is furnished by a dynamo generator,

name: scan0007-text-0208
text: mounted between the inclined camshaft drives at the

name: scan0007-text-0209
text: rear of the engine. This generator further charges the

name: scan0007-text-0210
text: accumulator. An auxiliary circuit breaker on each dis-

name: scan0007-text-0211
text: tributor head prevents the engine from firing in a reverse

name: scan0007-text-0212
text: direction.

name: scan0007-text-0213
text: Two duplex Zenith carburettors (type 52 D.F.) of

name: scan0007-text-0214
text: American manufacture are fitted on the engines now being

name: scan0007-text-0215
text: delivered, but later engines will be equipped with two

name: scan0007-text-0216
text: Claudel-Hobson carburettors, type H.C. 7.

name: scan0007-text-0217
text: An electric starter is to be fitted, for which a

name: scan0007-text-0218
text: special handbook will be published in due course.

name: scan0013-text-0676
text: General Description.

name: scan0013-text-0677
text: In the following descriptions, the propeller end of

name: scan0013-text-0678
text: the engine is termed the “front”; the words “right”

name: scan0013-text-0679
text: and “left” are used on the supposition that the engine

name: scan0013-text-0680
text: is viewed from the rear or distribution gear end.

name: scan0014-text-0685
text: CYLINDERS.

name: scan0014-text-0686
text: Each cylinder is formed from a steel tube, the head,

name: scan0014-text-0687
text: barrel, flange and spigot being all in one piece. One

name: scan0014-text-0688
text: end of the tube is closed down to form the cylinder head,

name: scan0014-text-0689
text: and seatings for the two valves are machined in it.

name: scan0014-text-0690
text: The holding-down flange is “jumped up” after local

name: scan0014-text-0691
text: heating, leaving a spigot 2

name: scan0014-text-0695
text: in. deep. The water jacket

name: scan0014-text-0696
text: is made of two sheet steel pressings, welded together:

name: scan0014-text-0697
text: the line of the main vertical joint is at right angles to

name: scan0014-text-0698
text: the crankshaft axis. There are further welded joints at

name: scan0014-text-0699
text: the two valve pockets, sparking plug bosses, upper and

name: scan0014-text-0700
text: lower water connections, camcase studs, and round the

name: scan0014-text-0701
text: base of the jacket.

name: scan0014-text-0702
text: The cylinders are interchangeable, though the long

name: scan0014-text-0703
text: and short studs supporting the camcase must be inter-

name: scan0014-text-0704
text: changed before a right-hand cylinder can be mounted in

name: scan0014-text-0705
text: the left-hand block and vice versâ. (See Fig. 2.)

name: scan0014-text-0706
text: The holding-down flanges are drilled for ten studs

name: scan0014-text-0707
text: apiece. Flats are cut through the two stud holes on

name: scan0014-text-0708
text: the fore and aft sides of each flange, so that the two studs

name: scan0014-text-0709
text: between a pair of cylinders secure both flanges. The

name: scan0014-text-0710
text: holding-down nuts are made with circular bases of

name: scan0014-text-0711
text: greater diameter than their hexagons.

name: scan0014-text-0712
text: Fig. 4.

name: scan0014-text-0713
text: Cylinder Head (plan view).

name: scan0015-text-0715
text: PISTONS.

name: scan0015-text-0716
text: Fig. 4 affords a plan view of a cylinder head, illus-

name: scan0015-text-0717
text: trating the large water space round each valve pocket

name: scan0015-text-0718
text: and the positions of the sparking plug bosses, camcase

name: scan0015-text-0719
text: studs, and water exit pipe: the latter is jointed by a

name: scan0015-text-0720
text: rubber connection to a short pipe projecting from the

name: scan0015-text-0721
text: water jacket of one of the four induction manifolds.

name: scan0015-text-0722
text: The circumference of each cylinder jacket increases

name: scan0015-text-0723
text: gradually towards the top of the piston stroke. The

name: scan0015-text-0724
text: water entry connections are short pipes, curving down-

name: scan0015-text-0725
text: wards from the base of each jacket on the outside of

name: scan0015-text-0726
text: the block.

name: scan0015-text-0727
text: The high compression pistons (Fig. 7) are of cast

name: scan0015-text-0728
text: aluminium alloy with externally domed tops, flattened

name: scan0015-text-0729
text: at the centre over a circle 2

name: scan0015-text-0733
text: in. in diameter. (The low

name: scan0015-text-0734
text: compression pistons have flat tops). There are no

name: scan0015-text-0735
text: internal ribs, but the crown is

name: scan0015-text-0739
text: in. thick, and the upper

name: scan0015-text-0740
text: part of the wall tapers down towards the gudgeon pin

name: scan0015-text-0741
text: bosses. There are three compression rings above the

name: scan0015-text-0742
text: Fig. 5.

name: scan0015-text-0743
text: Side View of a Cylinder.

name: scan0016-text-0745
text: gudgeon pin: each ring has a diagonal gap, and a

name: scan0016-text-0746
text: shallow circumferential oil groove is machined round

name: scan0016-text-0747
text: the centre of its working face. No scraper rings are

name: scan0016-text-0748
text: employed. Beneath the rings seven shallow oil grooves

name: scan0016-text-0749
text: are machined circumferentially on the outside of the

name: scan0016-text-0750
text: skirt, which is not drilled at any point.

name: scan0016-text-0751
text: Fig. 6.

name: scan0016-text-0752
text: Cylinder: Section through Valve Gear.

name: scan0017-text-0754
text: CONNECTING RODS.

name: scan0017-text-0755
text: The hollow steel gudgeon pin is parallel-sided, and

name: scan0017-text-0756
text: is a push fit in the bosses, which are cast on the skirt. It is

name: scan0017-text-0757
text: located endways by the two caps shown in Fig. 8.

name: scan0017-text-0758
text: Their outer faces are radiused to the contour of the

name: scan0017-text-0759
text: cylinder walls, and they are positioned in the bosses

name: scan0017-text-0760
text: by the rectangular projections shown in the photograph.

name: scan0017-text-0761
text: They were originally fixed by spring wire clips, which

name: scan0017-text-0762
text: have since been dispensed with. The holes in their

name: scan0017-text-0763
text: centres are threaded to take an extractor. The gudgeon

name: scan0017-text-0764
text: pin is allowed to float in the piston bosses and in the

name: scan0017-text-0765
text: small end bush.

name: scan0017-text-0766
text: The connecting rods are illustrated in Fig. 9. The

name: scan0017-text-0767
text: forked rods may be fitted on either side of the engine,

name: scan0017-text-0768
text: provided that they are all assembled on the same side.

name: scan0017-text-0769
text: The forked big ends grip a split phosphor bronze shell,

name: scan0017-text-0770
text: which is fixed in them by dowel pins, whilst annular

name: scan0017-text-0771
text: grooves machined on its exterior locate the forked rods

name: scan0017-text-0772
text: and prevent them from “spreading”; the caps are not

name: scan0017-text-0773
text: bridged. The shell is lined with white metal, and works

name: scan0017-text-0774
text: on the crank-pin in the usual way. The single rod works

name: scan0017-text-0775
text: Fig. 7.

name: scan0017-text-0776
text: Broken View of “Army” Piston.

name: scan0018-text-0778
text: on the outside of the phosphor bronze shell between the

name: scan0018-text-0779
text: forked ends of the double rod. The little ends are

name: scan0018-text-0780
text: bushed with phosphor bronze. Details of the lubrication

name: scan0018-text-0781
text: are given on page 36.

name: scan0018-text-0782
text: Fig. 8.

name: scan0018-text-0783
text: Pistons and Gudgeon Pins.

name: scan0018-text-0784
text: Fig. 9.

name: scan0018-text-0785
text: Connecting Rods.

name: scan0019-text-0787
text: CRANKSHAFT.

name: scan0019-text-0788
text: The crankshaft runs in seven bearings, consisting

name: scan0019-text-0789
text: of horizontally split phosphor bronze shells, lined with

name: scan0019-text-0790
text: white metal and housed in the crosswebs of the base

name: scan0019-text-0791
text: chamber. The bearing next the propeller is 115 mm. in

name: scan0019-text-0792
text: length, and the six rear bearings are 49 mm. long. The

name: scan0019-text-0793
text: ends of the journals and crankpins are sealed on early

name: scan0019-text-0794
text: engines by brass discs, soldered into position, but the

name: scan0019-text-0795
text: standard system will consist of steel caps, drawn up by

name: scan0019-text-0796
text: bolts. Details of the lubrication are given in Chapter II.

name: scan0019-text-0797
text: The main driving bevel is machined in one piece

name: scan0019-text-0798
text: with a starting claw, and is bolted to a flange machined

name: scan0019-text-0799
text: on the rear end of the shaft. Shims are threaded over

name: scan0019-text-0800
text: the bolts between the flange and the bevel for the pur-

name: scan0019-text-0801
text: pose of adjusting the mesh of the distribution gears.

name: scan0019-text-0802
text: The centre of the bevel is internally splined to provide

name: scan0019-text-0803
text: a drive for the gun interrupter gear.

name: scan0019-text-0804
text: Fig. 85, p. 114, illustrates in detail the double thrust

name: scan0019-text-0805
text: bearing, which is located between the propeller hub taper

name: scan0019-text-0806
text: and the front main bearing, and is provided with cast

name: scan0019-text-0807
text: housings in the base chamber. Its terminal stops con-

name: scan0019-text-0808
text: sist of a flange machined on the shaft, and a large flanged

name: scan0019-text-0809
text: and castellated nut, screwing on to a thread on the shaft.

name: scan0019-text-0810
text: Fig. 10.

name: scan0019-text-0811
text: Pair of Connecting Rods (dismantled).

name: scan0020-text-0813
text: BASE CHAMBER.

name: scan0020-text-0814
text: The maximum end play should not exceed .008 in.

name: scan0020-text-0815
text: The washers locating the thrust in the crankcase are

name: scan0020-text-0816
text: thick and thin respectively. They should be selected

name: scan0020-text-0817
text: so that when assembled they leave .001 in. end play in

name: scan0020-text-0818
text: the grooves in the crankcase.

name: scan0020-text-0819
text: The propeller hub is mounted by a taper and key

name: scan0020-text-0820
text: in the usual way. The key is fixed by a grubscrew at

name: scan0020-text-0821
text: its centre, fore and aft of which there are two threaded

name: scan0020-text-0822
text: holes in the key, by means of which the grubscrew may

name: scan0020-text-0823
text: be utilised to lift the key.

name: scan0020-text-0824
text: The locking device is illustrated in Fig. 77, p. 105.

name: scan0020-text-0825
text: The base chamber is made of two aluminium alloy

name: scan0020-text-0826
text: castings bolted together: the horizontal joint comes at

name: scan0020-text-0827
text: the level of the main bearing centres, as usual. There

name: scan0020-text-0828
text: are no “feet” or bearer brackets on the upper half: its

name: scan0020-text-0829
text: flange overhangs the lower half for the full length of

name: scan0020-text-0830
text: both sides, and is attached direct to the engine bearers

name: scan0020-text-0831
text: in the fuselage by seven bolts on each side. This pro-

name: scan0020-text-0832
text: jecting flange is stiffened by seven pairs of vertical ribs

name: scan0020-text-0833
text: on both sides.

name: scan0020-text-0834
text: Fig. 11.

name: scan0020-text-0835
text: Lower Half of Main Bearing.

name: scan0020-text-0836
text: Fig. 12.

name: scan0020-text-0837
text: Crankshaft Taper and Key.

name: scan0021-text-0002
text: Fig. 13.

name: scan0021-text-0003
text: Three-quarter Side View of Engine.

name: scan0022-text-0005
text: The main bearings are housed in the cross webs, so

name: scan0022-text-0006
text: that the crankshaft can be freed by unbolting the sump.

name: scan0022-text-0007
text: Similarly, the cylinders can be removed without dis-

name: scan0022-text-0008
text: turbing the crankshaft.

name: scan0022-text-0009
text: The two parts of the base chamber are secured

name: scan0022-text-0010
text: together by fifty small bolts distributed along the flange.

name: scan0022-text-0011
text: In addition, eight pairs of heavy studs are fixed in the

name: scan0022-text-0012
text: lower half along the centre line, two pairs at the front

name: scan0022-text-0013
text: bearing, and one pair at each of the six shorter bearings;

name: scan0022-text-0014
text: and two pairs of external bolts are employed at the ex-

name: scan0022-text-0015
text: treme front and rear ends of the base chamber respec-

name: scan0022-text-0016
text: tively.

name: scan0022-text-0017
text: Fig. 14.    Top Half of Crankcase.

name: scan0022-text-0018
text: Fig. 15.    Top Half of Crankcase, viewed from beneath.

name: scan0023-text-0020
text: The top half is cross-stiffened by eight webs, which

name: scan0023-text-0021
text: incorporate tubular housings for the studs above men-

name: scan0023-text-0022
text: tioned. The rear web and the two nose piece webs are

name: scan0023-text-0023
text: solid, but the other five webs have panels cut out of

name: scan0023-text-0024
text: them. The formation of the rear end is unusual, being

name: scan0023-text-0025
text: designed to provide a moisture-proof chamber for the

name: scan0023-text-0026
text: ball bearings of the distribution gears. This chamber

name: scan0023-text-0027
text: is enclosed by means of the rear wall and top end of the

name: scan0023-text-0028
text: casting, together with solid vertical and horizontal webs.

name: scan0023-text-0029
text: In the top of the compartment so formed there are four

name: scan0023-text-0030
text: apertures, respectively closed (when the engine is

name: scan0023-text-0031
text: assembled) by a breather cap, the vertical shaft, and the

name: scan0023-text-0032
text: two inclined shafts. In the base of the compartment

name: scan0023-text-0033
text: there are two apertures, closed respectively by the vertical

name: scan0023-text-0034
text: shaft and the oil trap shown in Fig. 87, p. 116. This trap

name: scan0023-text-0035
text: is kept permanently brimming with oil, which drains into

name: scan0023-text-0036
text: it from the casings of the inclined shafts. When con-

name: scan0023-text-0037
text: densed moisture is surging about in the main base

name: scan0023-text-0038
text: chamber under the influence of crankcase compression,

name: scan0023-text-0039
text: it can find no entry into the distribution gear compart-

name: scan0023-text-0040
text: ment, seeing that the oiltrap is sealed by oil. Thus the

name: scan0023-text-0041
text: ball races within the compartment are protected from

name: scan0023-text-0042
text: rust.

name: scan0023-text-0043
text: Two large breathers are bolted to the right-hand

name: scan0023-text-0044
text: side of the upper half of the base chamber. An en-

name: scan0023-text-0045
text: graved plate on the rear end gives the firing sequence

name: scan0023-text-0046
text: of the cylinders, and the name of the manufacturer.

name: scan0023-text-0047
text: Fig. 16.

name: scan0023-text-0048
text: Bottom Half of Crankcase.

name: scan0024-text-0050
text: Fig. 17.

name: scan0024-text-0051
text: Bottom Half of Crankcase, with Crankshaft in position.

name: scan0025-text-0053
text: VALVES.

name: scan0025-text-0054
text: The lower half of the base chamber is flat-bottomed,

name: scan0025-text-0055
text: with fore and aft oil wells. It is cast with cross webs

name: scan0025-text-0056
text: at each of the six shorter main bearings, and its nose

name: scan0025-text-0057
text: piece is heavily ribbed, both laterally and longitudinally,

name: scan0025-text-0058
text: to support the front main bearing. The lower half of

name: scan0025-text-0059
text: the housing for the thrust race is cast in the nose piece.

name: scan0025-text-0060
text: Towards the rear the casting is given an approximately

name: scan0025-text-0061
text: rectangular section, and houses the drive for the oil and

name: scan0025-text-0062
text: water pumps. The base of the sump is cast with a

name: scan0025-text-0063
text: narrow trough to accommodate the main pressure oil

name: scan0025-text-0064
text: pipe and the oil return pipe from the front oil well.

name: scan0025-text-0065
text: The lower halves of the main bearings are housed

name: scan0025-text-0066
text: in the cross webs, as stated above, and are not slung

name: scan0025-text-0067
text: in caps from bolts.

name: scan0025-text-0068
text: A cylindrical housing for the plain bearing of the

name: scan0025-text-0069
text: lower vertical shaft is cast as part of the lower half at

name: scan0025-text-0070
text: the rear end, immediately below the main crankshaft

name: scan0025-text-0071
text: bevel. The water pump unit is bolted to the rear end of

name: scan0025-text-0072
text: the sump, and driven by bevel gearing off the lower vertical

name: scan0025-text-0073
text: shaft. A splined extension of this shaft drives the oil

name: scan0025-text-0074
text: pumps, the oil pump unit being bolted beneath the rear

name: scan0025-text-0075
text: end of the sump.

name: scan0025-text-0076
text: Two straight steel oil pipes are inserted from the

name: scan0025-text-0077
text: rear end, and pushed through housings in the bases of

name: scan0025-text-0078
text: the cross webs. The right-hand pipe is the main supply

name: scan0025-text-0079
text: pipe, and communicates with the bottom centre of each

name: scan0025-text-0080
text: main bearing by means of a steel pipe screwed verti-

name: scan0025-text-0081
text: cally into each web; the supply for the camshaft is taken

name: scan0025-text-0082
text: from the front main bearing through a lead in the upper

name: scan0025-text-0083
text: half of the base chamber. Screwed plugs at either end

name: scan0025-text-0084
text: facilitate the cleaning of the main pressure pipe: the

name: scan0025-text-0085
text: forward plug is beneath the sump; the rear plug is

name: scan0025-text-0086
text: visible when the pump unit is dismounted. The left-

name: scan0025-text-0087
text: hand pipe connects the forward oil well to the scavenging

name: scan0025-text-0088
text: pump in the rear oil well. The front oil well contains

name: scan0025-text-0089
text: a filter: its cover is secured by a spring clip.

name: scan0025-text-0090
text: A felt oil-retaining washer is fitted at the front of the

name: scan0025-text-0091
text: nose piece.

name: scan0025-text-0092
text: The circular orifice opposite the rear end of the

name: scan0025-text-0093
text: crankshaft may be closed by a coverplate if a gun

name: scan0025-text-0094
text: interrupter gear or mechanical starter are not fitted.

name: scan0025-text-0095
text: There are two valves per cylinder, working in cast

name: scan0025-text-0096
text: iron guides pressed into the valve pockets. The valve

name: scan0025-text-0097
text: stems are inclined towards the cylinder axis at 13

name: scan0025-text-0101
text: °, the

name: scan0025-text-0102
text: exhausts being on the outside of each cylinder block, and

name: scan0025-text-0103
text: the inlets on the inside. The camcase is accommodated

name: scan0025-text-0104
text: within the included angle. All the valves are inter-

name: scan0025-text-0105
text: changeable, their smallest diameter measuring 63.5 mm.

name: scan0026-text-0107
text: Double concentric coiled springs are fitted. The

name: scan0026-text-0108
text: inner springs are interchangeable. The outer springs of

name: scan0026-text-0109
text: the inlet valves are longer than the corresponding

name: scan0026-text-0110
text: exhaust springs, which are of stouter gauge. A female

name: scan0026-text-0111
text: taper in the upper spring cap presses a pair of internally

name: scan0026-text-0112
text: Fig. 18.

name: scan0026-text-0113
text: Valve and Fittings.

name: scan0026-text-0114
text: Fig. 19.

name: scan0026-text-0115
text: Camshaft and Bearings.

name: scan0027-text-0117
text: CAMSHAFTS AND VALVE GEAR.

name: scan0027-text-0118
text: shouldered split cones against three annular grooves

name: scan0027-text-0119
text: machined on the valve stem.

name: scan0027-text-0120
text: The camshafts are not interchangeable, and are

name: scan0027-text-0121
text: marked “R” and “L” respectively. The camcases are

name: scan0027-text-0122
text: interchangeable.

name: scan0027-text-0123
text: They are machined in one piece, and drilled for

name: scan0027-text-0124
text: pressure lubrication, of which details are printed on p. 37.

name: scan0027-text-0125
text: The driven bevel pinions are bolted to flanges on the

name: scan0027-text-0126
text: rear ends of the shafts. Notched flanges or “hubs,”

name: scan0027-text-0127
text: secured to these studs behind the bevel pinions, drive the

name: scan0027-text-0128
text: rotating portions of the distributor heads.

name: scan0027-text-0129
text: Each camshaft runs in seven bushes (see Fig. 81,

name: scan0027-text-0130
text: p. 110), which are a driving fit in the camcase. They are

name: scan0027-text-0131
text: “stepped” in outside diameter, that at the rear end

name: scan0027-text-0132
text: being the largest, the next

name: scan0027-text-0136
text: in. smaller, etc. The five

name: scan0027-text-0137
text: intermediate bearings are cast in aluminium; they are

name: scan0027-text-0138
text: horizontally split, assembled by screws, and located in

name: scan0027-text-0139
text: the camcase by large grubscrews entered from the side.

name: scan0027-text-0140
text: The front bearing of each shaft is a one-piece cylindrical

name: scan0027-text-0141
text: bush of aluminium: the oil supply enters the camshaft

name: scan0027-text-0142
text: by this bush, as described on page 38. The rear bearing

name: scan0027-text-0143
text: is of special pattern, as illustrated in Fig. 81. It con-

name: scan0027-text-0144
text: sists of two phosphor bronze shells, lined with white

name: scan0027-text-0145
text: metal, and is mounted between two flanges machined on

name: scan0027-text-0146
text: the shaft, so as to take the thrust.

name: scan0027-text-0147
text: A camcase is illustrated in Fig. 20. It is an alu-

name: scan0027-text-0148
text: minium alloy casting, of tubular section between each

name: scan0027-text-0149
text: pair of cylinders, and widening into approximately

name: scan0027-text-0150
text: rectangular compartments with detachable lids over each

name: scan0027-text-0151
text: cylinder head. It is secured to each cylinder head by

name: scan0027-text-0152
text: a couple of studs.

name: scan0027-text-0153
text: Fig. 20.

name: scan0027-text-0154
text: Camcase.

name: scan0028-text-0156
text: DISTRIBUTION GEAR.

name: scan0028-text-0157
text: The inlet and exhaust rockers are machined from

name: scan0028-text-0158
text: steel forgings, different in shape for the right- and

name: scan0028-text-0159
text: left-hand sides of the cylinders, though either shape

name: scan0028-text-0160
text: may be used to operate the inlets or the exhausts. The

name: scan0028-text-0161
text: spindles are integral with the cam and valve arms. The

name: scan0028-text-0162
text: lower half of each rocker spindle bearing is machined

name: scan0028-text-0163
text: in the camcase, and the upper half in one of the re-

name: scan0028-text-0164
text: movable lids. The spindles are located endways in

name: scan0028-text-0165
text: their bearings by the valve-actuating arm at one end,

name: scan0028-text-0166
text: and at the other end by a flange turned on the spindle.

name: scan0028-text-0167
text: Two arms project from opposite sides of each spindle.

name: scan0028-text-0168
text: A short forked arm, projecting inwards near the centre

name: scan0028-text-0169
text: of the spindle, carries a hard steel roller which engages

name: scan0028-text-0170
text: the cam. A longer arm, projecting from the end of the

name: scan0028-text-0171
text: spindle, carries an adjustable bolt which actuates the

name: scan0028-text-0172
text: valve. The bolt has a square on it, which is a loose fit

name: scan0028-text-0173
text: in a square hole at the outer end of the arm: the bolt

name: scan0028-text-0174
text: is packed to the height required for correct valve clear-

name: scan0028-text-0175
text: ance by means of shim washers, and is then locked by

name: scan0028-text-0176
text: a castellated nut and split pin. The engines are delivered

name: scan0028-text-0177
text: with three shims of different thicknesses threaded on

name: scan0028-text-0178
text: each bolt.

name: scan0028-text-0179
text: Fig. 22 is a diagram of the general layout of the dis-

name: scan0028-text-0180
text: tribution gears. The main bevel on the crankshaft

name: scan0028-text-0181
text: drives upper and lower vertical shafts. The upper

name: scan0028-text-0182
text: vertical shaft drives the two inclined shafts which form

name: scan0028-text-0183
text: the camshaft drives; and its splined extension drives the

name: scan0028-text-0184
text: low tension generator. The lower vertical shaft drives

name: scan0028-text-0185
text: the horizontal water pump shaft through bevel gearing,

name: scan0028-text-0186
text: Fig. 21.

text: transmission at the base of the inclined shafts are all

name: scan0030-text-0221
text: of 22 teeth, so that all three shafts run at 1

name: scan0030-text-0227
text: the generator shaft by splines. For ease of assembly

name: scan0030-text-0228
text: and adjustment of mesh, each inclined shaft is arranged

name: scan0030-text-0229
text: in two pieces, coupled together by a splined joint at the

name: scan0030-text-0230
text: point of exit from the base chamber. The driving bevels

name: scan0030-text-0231
text: at the top of the inclined shafts have 16 teeth, and the

name: scan0030-text-0232
text: large driven camshaft bevels are of 48 teeth. As the

name: scan0030-text-0233
text: illustrations show, the upper vertical shaft runs in two

name: scan0030-text-0234
text: ball bearings. The short shafts at the base of the

name: scan0030-text-0235
text: inclined drives run in two ball bearings apiece. The

name: scan0030-text-0236
text: upper end of each long inclined shaft is provided with

name: scan0030-text-0237
text: a phosphor bronze bush, housed in the shaft casing.

name: scan0030-text-0238
text: A tachometer drive is taken off the generator shaft

name: scan0030-text-0239
text: by skew gearing, and runs at half engine speed.

name: scan0030-text-0240
text: The water pump is of the centrifugal type, its impeller

name: scan0030-text-0241
text: revolving in the vertical plane. The unit is bolted to

name: scan0030-text-0242
text: a circular aperture in the rear end of the sump, and its

name: scan0030-text-0243
text: spindle is driven through bevel gearing off the lower

name: scan0030-text-0244
text: vertical shaft at 1

name: scan0030-text-0248
text: times engine speed. The spindle is

name: scan0030-text-0249
text: supported by a ball bearing housed in the pump casing.

name: scan0030-text-0250
text: A double stuffing gland is provided on the engine side

name: scan0030-text-0251
text: of the impeller (Fig. 79, p. 108). Graphited asbestos is

name: scan0030-text-0252
text: wound round the shaft inside two sleeves; a star washer is

name: scan0030-text-0253
text: threaded on the shaft over each packing, and a spring

name: scan0030-text-0254
text: between the washers keeps the packings compressed;

name: scan0030-text-0255
text: the projections of the washers engage slots in the sleeves.

name: scan0030-text-0256
text: Supply pipes run from the two delivery ports of the

name: scan0030-text-0257
text: water pump towards the right- and left-hand sides of the

name: scan0030-text-0258
text: base-chamber respectively, and are coupled by rubber

name: scan0030-text-0259
text: connections to long water manifolds, lying along each

name: scan0030-text-0260
text: side of the engine below the cylinder base level. The

name: scan0031-text-0262
text: main pipes of these manifolds are tapered towards the

name: scan0031-text-0263
text: front of the engine; short branch pipes project upwards,

name: scan0031-text-0264
text: and are jointed to rubber connections by stub pipes

name: scan0031-text-0265
text: curving downwards from the base of each cylinder jacket.

name: scan0031-text-0266
text: The type of water clip employed throughout the Liberty

name: scan0031-text-0267
text: engine is illustrated on p. 119: its band is made of mild

name: scan0031-text-0268

name: scan0031-text-0269
text: The water return is taken through the induction

name: scan0031-text-0270
text: manifold jackets. There are four of these manifolds,

name: scan0031-text-0271
text: each serving a group of three cylinders. A short return

name: scan0031-text-0272
text: pipe in each cylinder head is jointed by rubber hose to

name: scan0031-text-0273
text: a pipe projecting from the adjacent inlet manifold. An

name: scan0031-text-0274
text: elbow is bolted down over the adjacent water exits of

name: scan0031-text-0275
text: the rear pair of manifolds, and a pipe runs forward to

name: scan0031-text-0276
text: a similar elbow uniting the water exits of the front pair

name: scan0031-text-0277
text: of manifolds. From the front elbow there is a single

name: scan0031-text-0278
text: return pipe to the radiator.

name: scan0031-text-0279

name: scan0031-text-0280

text: CHAPTER II.

name: scan0033-text-0296
text: OIL PUMPS.

name: scan0033-text-0297
text: The lubrication system is simple in outline, but

name: scan0033-text-0298
text: demands somewhat lengthy description, as some of the

name: scan0033-text-0299
text: individual units are complex. A large pump unit, con-

name: scan0033-text-0300
text: sisting of a three-pinion duplex scavenge pump mounted

name: scan0033-text-0301
text: above a pressure pump, is assembled in a casing bolted

name: scan0033-text-0302
text: beneath the rear end of the sump. Both pumps are

name: scan0033-text-0303
text: driven by a spindle which is jointed by splines to the

name: scan0033-text-0304
text: lower vertical shaft. The supply pump forces oil under

name: scan0033-text-0305
text: pressure along a manifold in the sump, which serves

name: scan0033-text-0306
text: all the main bearings. A lead from the front main

name: scan0033-text-0307
text: bearing conducts oil to a three-way branch at the front

name: scan0033-text-0308
text: of the base chamber, whence three pipes are connected

name: scan0033-text-0309
text: to the pressure gauge and the front ends of the two

name: scan0033-text-0310
text: camshafts respectively. The oil drains back to the sump

name: scan0033-text-0311
text: down the casings of the two inclined drives, lubricating

name: scan0033-text-0312
text: the bearings and pinions of the distribution gears on its

name: scan0033-text-0313
text: way. The pistons and gudgeon pins are lubricated by

name: scan0033-text-0314
text: splash.

name: scan0033-text-0315
text: The double scavenging pump is located in the pump

name: scan0033-text-0316
text: unit beneath the oil well at the rear end of the flat-

name: scan0033-text-0317
text: bottomed sump, and is connected by a pipe in the sump

name: scan0033-text-0318
text: to the oil well at the front end. Both oil wells are pro-

name: scan0033-text-0319
text: vided with filters, and their respective deliveries meet in

name: scan0033-text-0320
text: a common return pipe to the tank.

name: scan0033-text-0321
text: A detailed description of the various components

name: scan0033-text-0322
text: follows:—

name: scan0033-text-0323
text: It may be found difficult to grasp all the details

name: scan0033-text-0324
text: of the pump until it has actually been dismantled; it

name: scan0033-text-0325
text: is plentifully illustrated by sectioned and perspective

name: scan0033-text-0326
text: drawings in Figs. 24-29. The diagram in Fig. 25 and

name: scan0033-text-0327
text: the sectioned perspective in Fig. 24 are the simplest to

name: scan0033-text-0328
text: study, when the actual pump is not available.

name: scan0033-text-0329
text: As the section in Fig. 24 shows, the double scavenge

name: scan0033-text-0330
text: pump and single pressure pump, together with the filters

name: scan0033-text-0331
text: and relief valve, are accommodated in a casing, which is

name: scan0033-text-0332
text: bolted beneath the rear end of the sump; the main pres-

name: scan0033-text-0333
text: sure pipe and the return pipe from the front catchpit

name: scan0033-text-0334
text: are connected to the pumps via ducts drilled in the pump

name: scan0033-text-0335
text: casing. At the top of the unit is a phosphor bronze

name: scan0033-text-0336
text: bush, in which the driving spindle runs. The spindle

name: scan0033-text-0337
text: drives the centre pinion of the scavenging pump, and

name: scan0033-text-0338
text: passes through a steel partition into the driven pinion of

name: scan0033-text-0339
text: the lower or pressure pump. The loose gears are

name: scan0034-text-0341
text: mounted on steel spindles fixed in the casing. The oil

name: scan0034-text-0342
text: is filtered before entering either pump: the upper filter

name: scan0034-text-0343
text: is locked in position by a nut and tab washer: the lower

name: scan0034-text-0344
text: filter is secured by the bottom cover. The relief valve

name: scan0034-text-0345
text: is situated immediately outside the delivery port of the

name: scan0034-text-0346
text: pressure pump.

name: scan0034-text-0347
text: Fig. 25 is purely diagrammatic, and does not show

name: scan0034-text-0348
text: the actual disposition of the various parts and leads. At

name: scan0034-text-0349
text: A the supply pipe from the tank enters the filter chamber

name: scan0034-text-0350
text: surrounding the lower or pressure pump, into which

name: scan0034-text-0351
text: the oil passes at B. Oil under pressure emerges from

name: scan0034-text-0352
text: the pump at C, and enters the sump pressure manifold

name: scan0034-text-0353
text: at C1, passing on its way the relief valve D.

name: scan0034-text-0354
text: Turning to the scavenge pump, it must be remem-

name: scan0034-text-0355
text: bered that the sump is flat-bottomed, and that when the

name: scan0034-text-0356
text: aeroplane is diving or climbing, the drainage oil will run

name: scan0034-text-0357
text: exclusively into the front or rear oil well. The scavenge

name: scan0034-text-0358
text: pump consists of three pinions, driven by the centre

name: scan0034-text-0359
text: gear. It is therefore the equivalent of two separate

name: scan0034-text-0360
text: pumps, each composed of two gears: as its gears have

name: scan0034-text-0361
text: deeper teeth than the gears of the pressure pump, each

name: scan0034-text-0362
text: of its units is singly more powerful than the supply

name: scan0034-text-0363
text: pump.

name: scan0034-text-0364
text: If the aeroplane is diving, the drainage oil collecting

name: scan0034-text-0365
text: in the front catchpit will be sucked along the pipe E1

name: scan0034-text-0366
text: (Fig. 25), and enter one unit of the upper or scavenging

name: scan0034-text-0367
text: pump at E. The pump will deliver it into the main

name: scan0034-text-0368
text: return pipe to the tank at F. On the other hand, if

name: scan0038-text-0398
text: As there is a popular impression that gear pumps

name: scan0038-text-0399
text: will not exert strong suction, it may be of interest to

name: scan0038-text-0400
text: state that they suck oil quite efficiently over a much

name: scan0038-text-0401
text: greater distance than is required in this engine: but they

name: scan0038-text-0402
text: will only suck when they are primed. The two scavenge

name: scan0038-text-0403
text: pumps being formed of only three gear wheels, which-

name: scan0038-text-0404
text: ever pair is working at any moment keeps the remaining

name: scan0038-text-0405
text: wheel primed.

name: scan0038-text-0406
text: Figs. 27-30 show various sectioned views of the

name: scan0038-text-0407
text: pump, indicating the details of the various components

name: scan0038-text-0408
text: and ducts with accuracy. The only point requiring

name: scan0038-text-0409
text: further mention is the lead between the delivery port

name: scan0038-text-0410
text: of the pump unit scavenging the front oil well, and the

name: scan0038-text-0411
text: main return pipe: this lead consists of a duct machined

name: scan0038-text-0412
text: in the casing of the scavenge pump, crossing over the

name: scan0038-text-0413
text: top of the pump from one side to the other.

name: scan0038-text-0414
text: The relief valve is of the mushroom type; when an

name: scan0038-text-0415
text: excessive pressure is reached, the valve is forced from

name: scan0038-text-0416
text: its seating, and oil drains through the valve box back

name: scan0038-text-0417
text: into the casing, until the pressure sinks to the normal.

name: scan0038-text-0418
text: The bottom of the sump is cast with a narrow trough

name: scan0038-text-0419
text: along the centre line. This trough accommodates two

name: scan0038-text-0420
text: straight steel pipes, secured in housings at the cross

name: scan0038-text-0421
text: webs. The right-hand pipe is the main supply pipe: it

name: scan0038-text-0422
text: is pushed in from the rear end of the sump, and provided

name: scan0038-text-0423
text: with screwed plugs at both ends, so that it can easily

name: scan0038-text-0424
text: be cleansed. Vertical branch pipes, screwed into each of

name: scan0038-text-0425
text: the cross webs, connect it with the bottom centres of

name: scan0038-text-0426
text: the main bearings, in which the oil is distributed by suit-

name: scan0038-text-0427
text: able grooves, a supply being trapped by milled notches

name: scan0038-text-0428
text: in the white metal along the joints of the bearing on both

name: scan0038-text-0429
text: sides. At each bearing some of the oil enters the

name: scan0038-text-0430
text: crankshaft through a suitable hole, travels up the

name: scan0038-text-0431
text: rear web of the throw into the crank-pin, and is forced

name: scan0038-text-0432
text: out of another hole into the big end bearing. Suitable

name: scan0038-text-0433
text: grooves distribute oil over the crank-pin bearing, and

name: scan0039-text-0435
text: LUBRICATION OF THE GUDGEON PINS.

name: scan0039-text-0436
text: LUBRICATION OF THE CAMSHAFTS.

name: scan0039-text-0437
text: four holes, spaced out at 90°, allow oil to penetrate to

name: scan0039-text-0438
text: the centre of the outer circumference of the bush, on

name: scan0039-text-0439
text: which the single connecting rod oscillates.

name: scan0039-text-0440
text: The ends of the journals and crank-pins are sealed

name: scan0039-text-0441
text: by brass discs, tinned and sweated into position. Future

name: scan0039-text-0442
text: engines will have steel plugs drawn up by bolts.

name: scan0039-text-0443
text: The little end bushes are lubricated solely by splash,

name: scan0039-text-0444
text: the oil entering through a large hole drilled in the top

name: scan0039-text-0445
text: centre of the little end.

name: scan0039-text-0446
text: Fig. 31 illustrates the manner in which the camshaft

name: scan0039-text-0447
text: oil supply is taken from the front crankshaft bearing.

name: scan0039-text-0448
text: A branch from the pressure manifold in the sump delivers

name: scan0039-text-0449
text: oil into a longitudinal groove machined in the lower

name: scan0039-text-0450
text: housing of the bearing. This groove is connected by

name: scan0039-text-0451
text: circumferential grooves on both sides of the bearing to

name: scan0039-text-0452
text: a longitudinal groove in the upper housing, which con-

name: scan0039-text-0453
text: ducts the oil back to a vertical lead in the web of the

name: scan0039-text-0454
text: base chamber. Through this lead the oil reaches a

name: scan0039-text-0455
text: three-way connection on the top of the base chamber,

name: scan0039-text-0456
text: from which pipes are led to a pressure gauge and to the

name: scan0039-text-0457

name: scan0040-text-0464
text: camshafts.

name: scan0040-text-0465
text: The front end of each camcase is sealed by a screwed

name: scan0040-text-0466
text: cap, beneath which there is a C.A. washer: the oil pipe

name: scan0040-text-0467
text: is connected to the centre of the cap. The front cam-

name: scan0040-text-0468
text: shaft bearing is a cylindrical bush of aluminium: its

name: scan0040-text-0469
text: front end is sealed by a metal plate, attached to the bush

name: scan0040-text-0470
text: by four screws, and rendered oiltight by a paper washer.

name: scan0040-text-0471
text: Thus an oil recess is formed between the metal plate

name: scan0040-text-0472
text: and the screwed cap already mentioned. An oil duct is

name: scan0040-text-0473
text: machined in the thickness of the cylindrical bush, parallel

name: scan0040-text-0474
text: with its axis. The front end of this duct is open to the

name: scan0040-text-0475
text: oil chamber; the rear end of the duct turns at right-

name: scan0040-text-0476
text: angles, and opens into the centre of the bush, where it

name: scan0040-text-0477
text: registers once in each revolution with a hole drilled

name: scan0040-text-0478
text: through into the centre of the hollow camshaft. Oil

name: scan0040-text-0479
text: under pressure thus enters the camshaft, and is sprayed

name: scan0040-text-0480
text: out of holes positioned at the centres of the six remaining

name: scan0040-text-0481
text: bearings, along which it is distributed by suitable grooves.

name: scan0040-text-0482
text: There are no oil exits from the camshaft in the cam

name: scan0040-text-0483
text: compartments, but an ample supply of oil leaks along

name: scan0040-text-0484
text: the bearings into each compartment, and is splashed up

name: scan0040-text-0485
text: by the cams. The rocking lever spindles are hollow,

name: scan0040-text-0486
text: and drilled with one oil entry and three oil exits apiece,

name: scan0040-text-0487
text: their ends being plugged with brass. The oil entry is

name: scan0040-text-0488
text: above the point at which the roller arm joins the spindle:

name: scan0040-text-0489
text: a small baffle cast on the under side of the camcase lid

name: scan0040-text-0490
text: directs the oil splash into this hole, and it escapes into

name: scan0040-text-0491
text: the spindle bearing through the oil exits above men-

name: scan0040-text-0492
text: tioned.

name: scan0040-text-0493

name: scan0040-text-0494
